To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the erm(T) gene was identified in six strains of group B Streptoccus (GBS), which was harbored by a plasmid, and that the plasmid could be mobilized to other strains of GBS and to enterococci.
a novel plasmid harboring a small erm(T) resistance cassette was identified in GBS strains and that the plasmid could be transferred to both GBS and enterococci.
we identified six erythromycin-resistant GBS isolates carrying a 2,500-bp plasmid encoding the erm(T) gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the erm(T) plasmid, the first report of this plasmid in GBS, and the molecular characterization of the GBS erm(T)-positive strains.
the molecular characterization of GBS strains harboring the small erm(T)-carrying plasmids.
the identification of the erm(T) plasmid and its dissemination in France.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the erm(T) resistance is carried in the plasmid pGBS1 and is associated to a small number of GBS isolates.
GBS strains harboring the erm(T) resistance determinant in a small plasmid are not a major threat for public health.
the small plasmid carrying erm(T) is widespread in GBS strains and that it can be transferred to other GBS strains and E. faecalis strains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the small plasmid harboring erm(T) gene in GBS is a mobilizable plasmids, which can be transferred to other GBS and Enteroccoccus faecalis, thus promoting the spread of the erm(T) gene and the erythromycin resistance in the community.

we identified a novel small plasmid harboring erm(T) in six GBS strains, which could be mobilized to GBS and enterococcal strains, thus promoting a potential broad dissemination of the erm(T) resistance determinant.

the small erm(T)-carrying plasmids are a threat for the GBS population, and the presence of the erm(T) gene in GBS strains should be considered as a potential risk factor for the development of resistance against macrolide-lincosamide-streptogramin B antibiotics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single small mobilizable plasmids harbors erm(T) in GBS and that it can be easily transferred by mobilization, thus promoting the dissemination of erm(T) in this species.
the erm(T) gene is still circulating in GBS strains and that the mobilizable plasmids carrying the gene can easily spread among streptococci and enterococci.
the mobilizable plasmids carrying erm(T) are widespread among erythromycin-resistant GBS strains, and their transfer to other bacteria could promote their dissemination.
